# minuta

> Divide time into pieces: pure functions over plain, deeply readonly `Period` data (`{ start, end, unit }`, `start` included and `end` excluded) of Temporal values: `PlainDate` for year to day, `ZonedDateTime` for hour to second. The unit rules are plain data ("units").

## Rules

- Every unit-aware function exists twice: `xWith(units, …)` in `@aleksejdix/minuta/core` takes the units first; `x(…)` in `@aleksejdix/minuta` is the same function bound to `createUnits()`: weeks starting on Monday, moments in the runtime's zone. Where the runtime has no Temporal, `await temporalReady()` from `@aleksejdix/minuta/temporal` first. Unit-free functions have one form and take no units.
- `withUnits(units)` (from `@aleksejdix/minuta/core`) binds every core operation to your units, e.g. `withUnits(createUnits({ weekStartsOn: "sunday" }))`; the result's `units` are the units passed in. `calendar(units)` (`@aleksejdix/minuta/calendar`: grids, `isWeekday`, `isWeekend`) and `intervals(units)` (`@aleksejdix/minuta/intervals`: `gap`, `clamp`, `merge`, `split`, `resize`, `move`, `snap`) bind their entry's functions the same way.
- `Units` is a partial map of unit specs; pass only the units you use (`{ day, month }`) to keep the bundle small.
- No result is `undefined`, never `null` (`clamp` without overlap, `merge([])`, …).
- Invalid input throws `RangeError`; the message starts with one of the error codes below and says how to fix it.
- Nothing is mutated: every function returns new data.

## Error codes

- `INVALID_OPTION`: An option such as `step` or `maxPeriods` is not a positive whole number.
- `TOO_MANY_PERIODS`: `divideWith` would create more chunks than `maxPeriods` allows.
- `UNIT_NOT_SUPPORTED`: The `units` passed to a function have no spec for the requested unit.

## `@aleksejdix/minuta`

### `divide`

```ts
divide(period: Source, unit: Name, options: DivideOptions = {}): Chunks<Source, Name>
```

Split a period into chunks of `unit`, clipped to the period. Temporal units,
weeks start on Monday; `divideWith` in `minuta/core` takes your own units.

```ts
divide(period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-01"), "month"), "day"); // 31 day periods
divide(period(Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO(), "hour"), "minute", { step: 15 }); // 4 periods
```

### `duration`

```ts
duration(period: Period, unit: Unit): number
```

How many complete `unit`s fit into a period. Temporal units, calendar- and
DST-aware; `durationWith` in `minuta/core` takes your own units.

```ts
duration(period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-10-08"), "day"), "hour"); // 24
duration(period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-02-01"), "month"), "day"); // 28
```

### `next`

```ts
next(period: Source): Source
```

The next period of the same unit. Temporal units, weeks start on Monday.

```ts
next(period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15"), "month")); // April 2026
```

### `period`

```ts
period(value: TimeValue, unit: Name): PeriodOf<Name>
```

The period of `unit` that contains `value`. Temporal units, weeks start on
Monday, moments in the runtime's zone; `periodWith` in `minuta/core` takes
your own units.

```ts
period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15"), "month"); // { start: 2026-03-01, end: 2026-04-01, unit: "month" }
period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-18"), "week"); // Monday Mar 16 up to Monday Mar 23
```

### `previous`

```ts
previous(period: Source): Source
```

The previous period of the same unit. Temporal units, weeks start on Monday.

```ts
previous(period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15"), "month")); // February 2026
```

### `same`

```ts
same(first: Period, second: Period, unit: Unit | "custom"): boolean
```

Whether two periods fall into the same `unit`. Temporal units.

```ts
same(period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-16"), "day"), period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-20"), "day"), "week"); // true
```

### `shift`

```ts
shift(period: Source, steps: number): Source
```

Move a period by `steps` of its own unit; negative moves back. Temporal units.

```ts
shift(period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15"), "month"), 3); // June 2026
```

### `contains`

```ts
contains(period: Period, target: Target): boolean
```

Whether a period contains a date, a moment or another period. `end` is
excluded: March does not contain April 1. A date counts as its whole day;
next to a time period, dates become moments in that period's zone.

```ts
contains(march, Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-20")); // true
contains(march, Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-04-01")); // false
```

### `overlaps`

```ts
overlaps(first: Period, second: Period): boolean
```

Whether two periods share any time. Periods that only touch (one ends
where the other starts) do not overlap. Next to a time period, a date
period becomes moments in that period's zone.

```ts
overlaps(march, april); // false: they touch
overlaps(march, period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-31"), "week")); // true
```

### `range`

```ts
range(start: PlainDate, end: PlainDate): DatePeriod
range(start: ZonedDateTime, end: ZonedDateTime): TimePeriod
range(start: PlainDate | ZonedDateTime, end: PlainDate | ZonedDateTime): DatePeriod | TimePeriod
```

A custom period from `start` (included) to `end` (excluded). Forgiving:
values given in reverse order are swapped. Equal values make an empty
period.

```ts
range(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-01-01"), Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-04-01"));
// { start: 2026-01-01, end: 2026-04-01, unit: "custom" }: January to March
```

### `MinutaError`

Codes at the start of the messages of errors minuta throws.

### `MinutaErrorCode`

```ts
type MinutaErrorCode = (typeof MinutaError)[keyof typeof MinutaError];
```

One of the {@link MinutaError} codes.

### `Chunks`

```ts
type Chunks<
  Source extends Period,
  Name extends Unit,
> = Source extends DatePeriod
  ? Name extends DateUnit
    ? DatePeriod[]
    : TimePeriod[]
  : TimePeriod[];
```

The chunks a division makes: date periods when a date period is divided
by a date unit, time periods otherwise.

### `DivideOptions`

```ts
type DivideOptions = Readonly<{
  /** Maximum number of periods before throwing. Default: 100,000. */
  maxPeriods?: number | undefined;
  /** How many units each chunk spans. Default: 1. */
  step?: number | undefined;
}>;
```

Options for `divide` / `divideWith`.

### `Minuta`

```ts
type Minuta = Readonly<{
  contains: typeof contains;
  divide: <Source extends Period, Name extends Unit>(
    period: Source,
    unit: Name,
    options?: DivideOptions
  ) => Chunks<Source, Name>;
  duration: (period: Period, unit: Unit) => number;
  next: <Source extends Period>(period: Source) => Source;
  overlaps: typeof overlaps;
  period: <Name extends Unit>(value: TimeValue, unit: Name) => PeriodOf<Name>;
  previous: <Source extends Period>(period: Source) => Source;
  range: typeof range;
  same: (first: Period, second: Period, unit: Unit | "custom") => boolean;
  shift: <Source extends Period>(period: Source, steps: number) => Source;
  /** The units every member is bound to */
  units: Units;
}>;
```

All operations, bound to one set of units. Written out rather than
derived, so the generic signatures keep their type parameters: a day's
`period` is a `DatePeriod`, `next` of a `TimePeriod` a `TimePeriod`.

### `DatePeriod`

```ts
type DatePeriod = Readonly<{
  end: PlainDate;
  start: PlainDate;
  unit: DateUnit | "custom";
}>;
```

A span of calendar dates, `start` included and `end` excluded: March 2026
is `[2026-03-01, 2026-04-01)`. No time zone: a day is a date, so clock
changes cannot move it.

### `DateUnit`

```ts
type DateUnit = {
  [Name in Unit]: UnitRegistry[Name] extends "date" ? Name : never;
}[Unit];
```

The units made of calendar dates: `"year"` … `"day"`, and your own.

### `Period`

```ts
type Period = DatePeriod | TimePeriod;
```

The primitive: every time range is a Period. Plain, deeply readonly data,
`start` included and `end` excluded.

`periodWith(units, value, "month")` creates one aligned to a unit,
`range(start, end)` a custom one.

### `PeriodOf`

```ts
type PeriodOf<Name extends Unit> = Name extends DateUnit
  ? DatePeriod
  : TimePeriod;
```

The period a unit makes: a `DatePeriod` for date units, else a `TimePeriod`.

### `PlainDate`

```ts
type PlainDate = Readonly<Temporal.PlainDate>;
```

A calendar date, read-only.

### `TimePeriod`

```ts
type TimePeriod = Readonly<{
  end: ZonedDateTime;
  start: ZonedDateTime;
  unit: TimeUnit | "custom";
}>;
```

A span of moments in one time zone, `start` included and `end` excluded:
the hour from 13:00 is `[13:00, 14:00)`.

### `TimeUnit`

```ts
type TimeUnit = {
  [Name in Unit]: UnitRegistry[Name] extends "time" ? Name : never;
}[Unit];
```

The units made of moments: `"hour"`, `"minute"`, `"second"`, and your own.

### `TimeValue`

```ts
type TimeValue =
  | Readonly<Temporal.Instant>
  | PlainDate
  | Readonly<Temporal.PlainDateTime>
  | ZonedDateTime;
```

A value a period can be made from. Date units read its calendar date;
time units its moment, in the units' time zone unless it carries its own.

### `Unit`

```ts
type Unit = keyof UnitRegistry;
```

A unit name: `"year"`, `"quarter"`, `"month"`, `"week"`, `"day"`, `"hour"`,
`"minute"` or `"second"`, plus any unit added to `UnitRegistry`.

### `Units`

```ts
type Units = Readonly<{ [Name in Unit]?: SpecOf<Name> }> & Settings;
```

The unit specs available to unit-aware functions. Partial, so a bundle can
carry only the units it uses; `createUnits()` returns all, plus the
settings.

### `ZonedDateTime`

```ts
type ZonedDateTime = Readonly<Temporal.ZonedDateTime>;
```

A moment in a time zone, read-only.

### `Weekday`

```ts
type Weekday =
  | "friday"
  | "monday"
  | "saturday"
  | "sunday"
  | "thursday"
  | "tuesday"
  | "wednesday";
```

A day of the week by name.

## `@aleksejdix/minuta/core`

### `contains`

Same as `contains` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `divideWith`

```ts
divideWith(units: Units, period: Source, unit: Name, options: DivideOptions = {}): Chunks<Source, Name>
```

Divide a period into chunks of `unit`, clipped to the period. A date
period divided by a date unit gives date periods; divided by a time unit
(a day into hours), its days become moments in the units' time zone, so a
day the clocks skip has no hours at all.

```ts
divideWith(units, march, "day")                 // 31 day periods
divideWith(units, hour, "minute", { step: 15 }) // 4 fifteen-minute periods
```

### `durationWith`

```ts
durationWith(units: Units, period: Period, unit: Unit): number
```

How many complete `unit`s fit into a period, counted from its start with
the units' calendar and clock rules. A date period counted in a time unit
(a day in hours) becomes moments in the units' time zone first, so a day
the clocks change on has 23 or 25 hours.

```ts
durationWith(units, march, "day"); // 31
durationWith(units, period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-29"), "day"), "hour"); // 23 in Zurich
```

### `nextWith`

```ts
nextWith(units: Units, period: Source): Source
```

The next period of the same unit.

```ts
nextWith(units, march); // April
```

### `overlaps`

Same as `overlaps` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `periodWith`

```ts
periodWith(units: Units, value: TimeValue, unit: Name): PeriodOf<Name>
```

The period of `unit` that contains `value`. Date units read the value's
calendar date; time units its moment, in the units' time zone unless the
value carries its own.

```ts
periodWith(units, Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15"), "month");
// { start: 2026-03-01, end: 2026-04-01, unit: "month" }
periodWith(units, Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-15T10:30[Europe/Zurich]"), "hour");
// { start: 10:00, end: 11:00, unit: "hour" }
```

### `previousWith`

```ts
previousWith(units: Units, period: Source): Source
```

The previous period of the same unit.

```ts
previousWith(units, march); // February
```

### `range`

Same as `range` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `sameWith`

```ts
sameWith(units: Units, first: Period, second: Period, unit: Unit | "custom"): boolean
```

Whether two periods fall into the same `unit`, compared by their starts:
the same calendar unit for date units, the same moment's unit for time
units. With `"custom"`, both edges must be identical.

```ts
sameWith(units, mondayPeriod, fridayPeriod, "week") // true
```

### `shiftWith`

```ts
shiftWith(units: Units, period: Source, steps: number): Source
```

Move a period by `steps` of its own unit: the period that many places
after (or before) it, so shifting by n is n times `next`. A custom period
moves by its own length.

```ts
shiftWith(units, march, 2)  // May
shiftWith(units, march, -1) // February
```

### `createUnits`

```ts
createUnits(options: UnitsOptions = {}): AllUnits
```

Unit specs for every unit, computed with the TC39 Temporal API: date
units on `PlainDate`, time units on `ZonedDateTime`. Pass the result to
`withUnits`, `calendar`, `intervals` or any `…With` function. Weeks
start on Monday unless `weekStartsOn` says otherwise (`"sunday"` …
`"saturday"`, or 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday); `weekend` sets
the days `isWeekend` counts (Saturday and Sunday unless set); `locale`
takes both from a locale's week (`Intl.Locale#getWeekInfo`); `timeZone`
is where dates become moments; `calendar` the calendar dates are read in. Where the runtime has no Temporal,
`await temporalReady()` first.

```ts
import { createUnits, withUnits } from "@aleksejdix/minuta/core";

const time = withUnits(createUnits({ timeZone: "UTC", weekStartsOn: "sunday" }));
time.period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-18"), "week"); // [Mar 15, Mar 22)

createUnits({ locale: "ar-EG" }).weekend; // [5, 6]: Friday and Saturday
```

### `UnitsOptions`

```ts
type UnitsOptions = WeekOptions &
  Readonly<{
    /**
     * IANA time zone that dates become moments in, e.g. when a day is
     * divided into hours: `"UTC"`, `"Europe/Zurich"`. Default: the runtime's.
     */
    timeZone?: string | undefined;
    /**
     * Temporal calendar every date is read in, e.g. `"hebrew"`,
     * `"islamic-umalqura"`, `"persian"`. Default: each date keeps its own
     * calendar (ISO 8601 for dates made from moments).
     */
    calendar?: string | undefined;
  }>;
```

Options of `createUnits`: the week, the weekend and the time zone.

### `MinutaError`

Same as `MinutaError` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `specFor`

```ts
specFor(units: Units, unit: Name): SpecOf<Name>
```

The spec for `unit`.

```ts
specFor(createUnits(), "week").startOf(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-18")); // 2026-03-16, a Monday
```

### `MinutaErrorCode`

Same as `MinutaErrorCode` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `withUnits`

```ts
withUnits(units: Units): Minuta
```

Bind every operation to `units`. Pass only the units you need, or the
full set of `createUnits()`. For the calendar and interval functions, use
`calendar(units)` and `intervals(units)` from their entries.

```ts
import { createUnits, withUnits } from "@aleksejdix/minuta/core";

const time = withUnits(createUnits({ weekStartsOn: "sunday" }));
time.next(time.period(Temporal.Now.plainDateISO(), "week"));
time.units; // the units passed in
```

### `Chunks`

Same as `Chunks` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `DivideOptions`

Same as `DivideOptions` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `Minuta`

Same as `Minuta` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `WeekOptions`

```ts
type WeekOptions = Readonly<{
  /**
   * Locale whose week to follow: its first day and its weekend, as
   * `Intl.Locale#getWeekInfo` gives them (`"en-US"` starts on Sunday,
   * `"ar-EG"` on Saturday with a Friday–Saturday weekend). `weekStartsOn`
   * and `weekend` win over it. Default: none, the ISO 8601 week.
   */
  locale?: string | undefined;
  /** First day of the week. Default: `"monday"` (ISO 8601), or the locale's. */
  weekStartsOn?: Weekday | WeekdayNumber | undefined;
  /** Days that `isWeekend` counts as weekend. Default: `["saturday", "sunday"]`, or the locale's. */
  weekend?: readonly (Weekday | WeekdayNumber)[] | undefined;
}>;
```

Week options of `createUnits`.

### `Weekday`

Same as `Weekday` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `WeekdayNumber`

```ts
type WeekdayNumber =
  | typeof SUNDAY
  | typeof MONDAY
  | typeof TUESDAY
  | typeof WEDNESDAY
  | typeof THURSDAY
  | typeof FRIDAY
  | typeof SATURDAY;
```

A day of the week as a number: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday.

### `AllUnits`

```ts
type AllUnits = Readonly<{ [Name in BuiltInUnit]: SpecOf<Name> }> &
  Readonly<{ timeZone: string }> &
  Settings;
```

A spec for every built-in unit, as `createUnits()` returns. Add specs of
your own units next to them: `Object.assign({ fortnight }, createUnits())`.

### `BuiltInUnit`

```ts
type BuiltInUnit =
  | "day"
  | "hour"
  | "minute"
  | "month"
  | "quarter"
  | "second"
  | "week"
  | "year";
```

The units every set of units provides. Units added to `UnitRegistry` come
with your own spec, so they are not part of `AllUnits`.

### `DatePeriod`

Same as `DatePeriod` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `DateSpec`

```ts
type DateSpec = Readonly<{
  /** Marks a spec of calendar dates */
  kind: "date";
  add: (date: PlainDate, amount: number) => PlainDate;
  diff: (from: PlainDate, to: PlainDate) => number;
  startOf: (date: PlainDate) => PlainDate;
}>;
```

How one date unit behaves on calendar dates — plain data.

- startOf: the first date of the unit containing `date`
- add(date, n): the date `n` units later (negative: earlier)
- diff(from, to): the number of complete units from `from` to `to`,
  truncated toward zero: the largest `n` with `add(from, n) <= to` (for
  an earlier `to`, the smallest `n` with `add(from, n) >= to`)

### `DateUnit`

Same as `DateUnit` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `Period`

Same as `Period` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `PeriodOf`

Same as `PeriodOf` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `PlainDate`

Same as `PlainDate` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `Settings`

```ts
type Settings = Readonly<{
  /**
   * IANA time zone that dates become moments in, e.g. when a day is divided
   * into hours. Default: the runtime's.
   */
  timeZone?: string | undefined;
  /** First day of the `week` spec, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Default: Monday. */
  weekStartsOn?: WeekdayNumber | undefined;
  /** Weekend days, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Default: Saturday and Sunday. */
  weekend?: readonly WeekdayNumber[] | undefined;
}>;
```

Settings that travel with the unit specs.

### `SpecOf`

```ts
type SpecOf<Name extends Unit> = Name extends DateUnit ? DateSpec : TimeSpec;
```

The spec of a unit: a `DateSpec` for date units, else a `TimeSpec`.

### `TimePeriod`

Same as `TimePeriod` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `TimeSpec`

```ts
type TimeSpec = Readonly<{
  /** Marks a spec of moments */
  kind: "time";
  add: (date: ZonedDateTime, amount: number) => ZonedDateTime;
  diff: (from: ZonedDateTime, to: ZonedDateTime) => number;
  startOf: (date: ZonedDateTime) => ZonedDateTime;
}>;
```

How one time unit behaves on moments, with the same contract as
`DateSpec`. Results stay in the zone of the value passed in.

### `TimeUnit`

Same as `TimeUnit` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `TimeValue`

Same as `TimeValue` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `Unit`

Same as `Unit` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `UnitRegistry`

Registry of unit names and their kind: `"date"` units (a year … a day)
are made of calendar dates, `"time"` units (an hour … a second) of
moments in a time zone. An interface so your code can add units through
module augmentation; the matching spec is passed as data in `Units`.

### `Units`

Same as `Units` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

### `ZonedDateTime`

Same as `ZonedDateTime` in `@aleksejdix/minuta`.

## `@aleksejdix/minuta/calendar`

### `calendar`

```ts
calendar(units: Units): Calendar
```

Bind the calendar functions to `units`: `monthGrid(date)` instead of
`monthGridWith(units, date)`.

```ts
const grids = calendar(createUnits({ weekStartsOn: "sunday" }));
grids.monthGrid(Temporal.Now.plainDateISO()); // 6 weeks, from a Sunday
grids.isWeekend(period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-21"), "day")); // true
```

### `dayGridWith`

```ts
dayGridWith(units: Units, value: TimeValue): DayGrid
```

The real hours of the day containing `value`: 23 on a spring-forward day,
25 on a fall-back day, 24 otherwise. The day lies in the zone of a moment
passed in, else in the units' time zone; each slot carries the wall-clock
hour it starts in.

```ts
import { dayGridWith } from "@aleksejdix/minuta/calendar";

const units = createUnits({ timeZone: "America/New_York" });
const { periods, gapHour } = dayGridWith(units, Temporal.PlainDate.from("2024-03-10"));
periods.length; // 23
gapHour; // 2
```

### `monthGridWith`

```ts
monthGridWith(units: Units, value: TimeValue): MonthGrid
```

A stable month grid: 42 day periods (6 weeks) starting with the week that
contains the first of the month. The week start comes from the `week` unit.

```ts
const { periods } = monthGridWith(createUnits({ weekStartsOn: "monday" }), Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15"));
```

### `yearGridWith`

```ts
yearGridWith(units: Units, value: TimeValue): YearGrid
```

A stable year grid: whole weeks from the week containing January 1 to the
week containing December 31. The week start comes from the `week` unit.

```ts
yearGridWith(createUnits({ weekStartsOn: "monday" }), Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-06-01")).periods; // 53 week periods
```

### `isWeekdayWith`

```ts
isWeekdayWith(units: Units, period: Period): boolean
```

Whether every day the period touches is a working day: not in the units'
`weekend` (Saturday and Sunday unless set).

```ts
isWeekdayWith(createUnits(), period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-18"), "day")); // true (a Wednesday)
isWeekdayWith(createUnits({ weekend: ["friday", "saturday"] }), period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-22"), "day")); // true (a Sunday)
```

### `isWeekendWith`

```ts
isWeekendWith(units: Units, period: Period): boolean
```

Whether every day the period touches is a weekend day, as configured by
the units' `weekend` (Saturday and Sunday unless set).

```ts
isWeekendWith(createUnits(), period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-21"), "day")); // true (a Saturday)
isWeekendWith(createUnits({ weekend: ["friday", "saturday"] }), period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-20"), "day")); // true (a Friday)
```

### `Calendar`

```ts
type Calendar = Readonly<{
  dayGrid: (value: TimeValue) => DayGrid;
  isWeekday: (period: Period) => boolean;
  isWeekend: (period: Period) => boolean;
  monthGrid: (value: TimeValue) => MonthGrid;
  yearGrid: (value: TimeValue) => YearGrid;
}>;
```

The calendar functions, bound to one set of units.

### `DayGrid`

```ts
type DayGrid = Readonly<{
  /** The hour slots of the day */
  periods: readonly HourSlot[];
  /** Wall-clock hour that doesn't exist due to spring forward, or undefined */
  gapHour: number | undefined;
  /** Wall-clock hour that occurs twice due to fall back, or undefined */
  ambiguousHour: number | undefined;
}>;
```

The real hours of a day: 23, 24 or 25 slots, with the skipped and the
repeated wall-clock hour.

### `HourSlot`

```ts
type HourSlot = TimePeriod &
  Readonly<{
    /** Wall-clock hour (0-23) the slot starts in, in the day's zone */
    hour: number;
  }>;
```

One real hour of a day, labelled with its wall-clock hour.

### `MonthGrid`

```ts
type MonthGrid = Readonly<{
  monthStart: PlainDate;
  /** The 42 day periods, row by row */
  periods: readonly DatePeriod[];
  /** The weekday the grid starts on, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday */
  weekStartsOn: number;
}>;
```

A 42-day month grid (`periods`), the month's first day and the week start
the grid was built with.

### `YearGrid`

```ts
type YearGrid = Readonly<{
  /** The week periods covering the year */
  periods: readonly DatePeriod[];
  /** The weekday the grid starts on, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday */
  weekStartsOn: number;
  yearStart: PlainDate;
}>;
```

The whole weeks covering a year (`periods`), the year's first day and the
week start the grid was built with.

## `@aleksejdix/minuta/intervals`

### `intervals`

```ts
intervals(units: Units): Intervals
```

Bind the interval functions to `units`: `merge(periods)` and
`snap(value, unit)` instead of `mergeWith(units, …)` and
`snapWith(units, …)`. The unit-free ones come along unchanged.

```ts
const edit = intervals(createUnits());
edit.snap(Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-15T10:37[Europe/Zurich]"), "minute", { step: 15 }); // 10:30
edit.merge(days, "month"); // one period, if the days touch
```

### `clamp`

```ts
clamp(period: Period, bounds: Period): Period | undefined
```

Constrain a period to fit within bounds: the time the two share.

Returns undefined when they share no time, also when they only touch.
Next to a time period, a date period becomes moments in that period's
zone.

```ts
const selection = range(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-01-05"), Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-01-25"));
const allowed = range(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-01-10"), Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-01-20"));
clamp(selection, allowed);
// → { start: 2026-01-10, end: 2026-01-20, unit: "custom" }
```

### `gap`

```ts
gap(from: TimePoint, to: TimePoint): Period | undefined
```

The time between two dates, moments or periods: from where the earlier
one ends to where the later one starts. A date counts as its whole day, a
moment as an instant. Order does not matter.

```ts
gap(period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-02"), "day"), period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-05"), "day"));
// { start: 2026-03-03, end: 2026-03-05, unit: "custom" }: Mar 3 and 4
gap(period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-02"), "day"), period(Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-03"), "day")); // undefined: they touch
```

### `mergeWith`

```ts
mergeWith(units: Units, periods: readonly Source[], unit?: Unit): Source | undefined
```

Merge periods of one kind into one spanning the earliest start to the
latest end. The result keeps `unit` (by default the first period's unit)
only when it is exactly one period of that unit; otherwise its unit is
`"custom"`.

```ts
mergeWith(units, [januaryFirstHalf, januarySecondHalf], "month"); // January, unit "month"
mergeWith(units, [january, march]); // Jan 1 – Apr 1, unit "custom"
mergeWith(units, []); // undefined
```

### `move`

```ts
move(period: DatePeriod, target: PlainDate): DatePeriod
move(period: TimePeriod, target: ZonedDateTime): TimePeriod
move(period: Period, target: PlainDate | ZonedDateTime): Period
```

Relocate a period to start at `target`, keeping its length: days for a
date period, exact time for a time period.

```ts
const appointment = range(Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-29T09:00[Europe/Zurich]"), Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-29T10:00[Europe/Zurich]"));
move(appointment, Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-04-02T14:00[Europe/Zurich]"));
// → { start: Apr 2 14:00, end: Apr 2 15:00, unit: "custom" }
```

### `resize`

```ts
resize(period: DatePeriod, edge: "start" | "end", value: PlainDate): DatePeriod | undefined
resize(period: TimePeriod, edge: "start" | "end", value: ZonedDateTime): TimePeriod | undefined
resize(period: Period, edge: "start" | "end", value: PlainDate | ZonedDateTime): Period | undefined
```

Move one edge of a period while keeping the other fixed.

Returns undefined if the new edge crosses the fixed edge. Meeting it is
fine: the result is an empty period.

```ts
const meeting = range(Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-29T09:00[Europe/Zurich]"), Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-29T10:00[Europe/Zurich]"));
resize(meeting, "end", Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-29T11:30[Europe/Zurich]"));
// → { start: 9:00, end: 11:30, unit: "custom" }
```

### `snapWith`

```ts
snapWith(units: Units, value: PlainDate, unit: DateUnit, options?: SnapOptions): PlainDate
snapWith(units: Units, value: ZonedDateTime, unit: Unit, options?: SnapOptions): ZonedDateTime
snapWith(units: Units, value: PlainDate | ZonedDateTime, unit: Unit, options?: SnapOptions): PlainDate | ZonedDateTime
```

Snap a date or a moment to a boundary of `step` units: the unit's start,
or every `step`-th one counted from the start of the enclosing unit
(minutes from the hour, hours from the day, days from the month, months
and quarters from the year; weeks and years from 1970). A date snaps to
dates; a moment snaps to moments in its zone, for date units to the start
of a day.

```ts
snapWith(units, Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-15T10:37[Europe/Zurich]"), "minute", { step: 15 }); // 10:30
snapWith(units, Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from("2026-03-15T10:37[Europe/Zurich]"), "day", { mode: "ceil" }); // Mar 16 00:00
snapWith(units, Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-18"), "week", { mode: "floor" }); // 2026-03-16
```

### `split`

```ts
split(period: DatePeriod, at: PlainDate): [DatePeriod, DatePeriod] | undefined
split(period: TimePeriod, at: ZonedDateTime): [TimePeriod, TimePeriod] | undefined
split(period: Period, at: PlainDate | ZonedDateTime): [Period, Period] | undefined
```

Split a period where the second part starts. Both parts are `"custom"`
periods: half a month is not a month. The first part ends where the
second begins, so every moment belongs to exactly one of them.

```ts
split(march, Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-03-15"));
// [2026-03-01 – 2026-03-15, 2026-03-15 – 2026-04-01]
split(march, Temporal.PlainDate.from("2027-01-01")); // undefined
```

### `Intervals`

```ts
type Intervals = Readonly<{
  clamp: typeof clamp;
  gap: typeof gap;
  merge: <Source extends Period>(
    periods: readonly Source[],
    unit?: Unit
  ) => Source | undefined;
  move: typeof move;
  resize: typeof resize;
  snap: Snap;
  split: typeof split;
}>;
```

The interval functions, the unit-aware ones bound to one set of units.

### `Snap`

```ts
type Snap = {
  (value: PlainDate, unit: DateUnit, options?: SnapOptions): PlainDate;
  (value: ZonedDateTime, unit: Unit, options?: SnapOptions): ZonedDateTime;
};
```

`snapWith` once bound: a date snaps to dates, a moment to moments.

### `SnapMode`

```ts
type SnapMode = "ceil" | "floor" | "nearest";
```

How `snap` / `snapWith` picks the boundary.

### `SnapOptions`

```ts
type SnapOptions = Readonly<{
  /** `"floor"`, `"ceil"` or `"nearest"` (ties round up). Default: `"nearest"`. */
  mode?: SnapMode | undefined;
  /** How many units lie between boundaries. Default: 1. */
  step?: number | undefined;
}>;
```

Options for `snap` / `snapWith`.

## `@aleksejdix/minuta/format`

### `formatPeriod`

```ts
formatPeriod(period: Period, locale: string, options: DisplayOptions = {}): string
```

Format a period as a locale-aware display string, picking the right
format for its unit: a weekday and a day for a day, the month and year
for a month, a range for weeks and custom periods. The same text
everywhere: on native Temporal and the polyfill, on a server and in the
browser.

```ts
formatPeriod(march, "de-CH"); // "März 2026"
formatPeriod(day, "en-US"); // "March 15, 2026"
formatPeriod(day, "en-US", { weekday: "short" }); // "Sun"
formatPeriod(week, "ja-JP"); // "2026/03/09～2026/03/15"
```

### `formatRange`

```ts
formatRange(period: Period, locale: string, options: DisplayOptions = {}): string
```

Format a period as a locale-aware range string, collapsing shared parts
(same year, same month) with `Intl.DateTimeFormat#formatRange`. A date
period shows its first and its last day; a time period its start and its
end. The same text everywhere: on native Temporal and the polyfill, on a
server and in the browser.

```ts
formatRange(march, "de-CH"); // "1.–31. März 2026"
formatRange(lastWeekOfMarch, "de-CH"); // "30. März – 5. Apr. 2026"
formatRange(hour, "en-US"); // "Mar 18, 10:00 – 11:00 AM"
```

## `@aleksejdix/minuta/temporal`

### `temporalReady`

```ts
temporalReady(): Promise<void>
```

Make Temporal available before minuta computes with it. Does nothing where
the runtime has Temporal (Chrome and Edge 144+, Firefox 139+, Node 26+);
elsewhere it loads `temporal-polyfill` in its own chunk and installs it
on `globalThis`. Await it once, before anything renders.

```ts
import { createUnits } from "@aleksejdix/minuta/core";
import { temporalReady } from "@aleksejdix/minuta/temporal";

await temporalReady();
const units = createUnits();
```
